title: Sewer failure & toilets without service
summary: Stop using plumbing that is backing up or may discharge sewage into living areas. Keep children and pets away from contaminated water. Separate toilet waste from drinking water, food and washing areas, and use a contained temporary toilet arrangement until safe disposal and service are established. Do not flush blindly during a sewer disruption.
text: Stop using plumbing that is backing up or may discharge sewage into living areas. Keep children and pets away from contaminated water. Separate toilet waste from drinking water, food and washing areas, and use a contained temporary toilet arrangement until safe disposal and service are established. Do not flush blindly during a sewer disruption.  Can I flush if I have a bucket of water? Only if the plumbing and wastewater system are usable and there is no relevant restriction. Extra water can worsen backup when drainage has failed. Establish the system status before adding it. Can contained human waste go in ordinary rubbish? Do not assume so. Check what the actual local collection or disposal arrangement accepts, including the container and product requirements. Secure containment buys time but does not create a legal or safe disposal route. Water supply and wastewater service are different A toilet that has no flushing water is not the same as a toilet connected to a damaged or backed-up sewer. Identify whether the problem is water supply, drainage, the building’s internal plumbing, a septic system, or a wider wastewater failure. Do not keep pouring water into a toilet to test it when sewage may back up or service is restricted. The first sanitation decisions Stop adding water When drains back up or a sewer restriction applies, stop using affected plumbing. Protect the clean area Keep people away from sewage and separate drinking water, food, and care supplies. Arrange the alternative Use a suitable contained toilet option with handwashing and a verified waste plan. Editorial response map. It does not diagnose the plumbing or authorize disposal into a damaged system. Check utility or property-management information when reachable and record the affected systems and restrictions. In a shared building, your sink may connect to a wider problem. A neighbor’s toilet working once does not establish that the whole drainage system is safe. Significant sewage contamination requires qualified assessment and cleanup. Set a boundary around contamination Keep children, pets, food, and clean water out of affected areas. Avoid touching or walking through sewage, especially where electrical equipment or building damage may also be involved. Do not enter standing water to operate electrical switches or appliances. A bleach solution does not make a sewage flood safe to enter. Keep these functions separate Function What to protect Drinking water and food Closed clean containers, meal surfaces, utensils, and suitable preparation water. Personal and medical care Clean supplies, appropriate handwashing, and a usable care space. Temporary toilet A stable private arrangement separated from meals and clean supply storage. Waste containment Leak-resistant closed storage, protected from access and away from water sources. Cleanup Qualified assistance for substantial contamination; no unsafe entry to begin the task. For a small household, draw the actual room layout and identify where each function can take place. If there is no way to keep living and care areas clear of contamination, staying may not be workable. Do not hide that problem behind an inventory showing plenty of food and batteries. Choose a temporary toilet for the user and setting A purpose-made portable toilet can provide a contained option when used according to its instructions. Check the seat stability, user capacity, cleaning requirements, liners or chemicals specified by the product, and the actual disposal route. A portable toilet is not complete simply because someone can sit on it. Choose a stable, accessible position with appropriate privacy and lighting; keep it away from food and drinking-water storage. Check how a person with limited mobility transfers, reaches supplies, and receives assistance. Do not improvise an unstable seat or unsafe lifting routine. Keep required consumables and instructions together. Different toilet systems may use different waste-handling arrangements. Keep the setup secured from children and pets, with a responsible adult managing used materials. Use local public-health sanitation guidance for improvised alternatives and disposal. Do not assume another state’s emergency method is permitted in your location. If an improvised contained arrangement is the only immediate option, it still needs stability, appropriate leak-resistant containment, privacy, handwashing, and a plan for secure temporary holding. This guide does not provide a universal construction or waste-treatment recipe. Where those conditions cannot be met, prioritize a safer sanitation location. Make waste handling and handwashing one task Prepare the handwashing area before handling waste. Use suitable water and soap, and arrange runoff without relying on failed drains. CDC recommends washing hands for at least 20 seconds. Gloves can reduce contact during handling but do not replace handwashing or remove the need to keep clean supplies separate. Prepare needed containment and cleaning supplies without placing them in the food area. Follow the toilet’s actual procedure and local sanitation instructions for closing and handling used materials. Prevent leaks and keep the closed waste container protected from access. Clean the appropriate surfaces with suitable products according to their instructions; never mix chemicals. Remove used gloves appropriately, then wash hands before returning to food or care tasks. Assign the dirty task to a capable adult where possible, and keep the routine simple enough that another adult can understand it. The person assisting a dependent household member may need separate help to handle waste. Do not rely on a child to recognize contamination or carry a heavy used container. A disposal plan is essential Confirm what the local wastewater utility, public-health service, or emergency collection arrangement accepts and where. Keep the instructions, opening status, transport requirement, and contact details. Rules for human waste, portable-toilet chemicals, diapers, and ordinary rubbish may differ. An ordinary collection vehicle passing the street does not authorize every waste type. Questions for a verified disposal route Question Why it matters What waste is accepted? Different products and waste streams may require different handling. What container or closure is required? Leak prevention and acceptance requirements may be specific. Is the site or service operating? A normal-service directory may be outdated during disruption. How can it be transported safely? Do not contaminate people, care supplies, or drinking water in transit. What if collection is delayed? Secure temporary holding has limits; arrange another sanitation location before capacity fails. Do not discharge waste into streets, storm drains, rivers, or open ground. Do not invent a burial or chemical-treatment solution without appropriate local guidance. If collection is unavailable, maintain secure contained holding while seeking a verified option. If the dwelling cannot sustain it safely, reconsider remaining there. Restart service and review what failed Water pressure returning does not prove that the sewer or septic system is ready. Confirm the applicable instructions before resuming use. Arrange qualified assessment where there was damage or significant contamination. A normal-looking drain should not override a continuing service restriction. Confirm the status of wastewater service and the building’s affected plumbing. Keep contaminated materials and cleanup tasks separated from normal living and meal preparation. Follow the applicable cleanup and disposal instructions; use qualified help for significant contamination. Replenish toilet, handwashing, and personal-care consumables. Record the usable capacity and limitations of the temporary arrangement. Update the relocation trigger if the household could not maintain safe sanitation. For a preparedness exercise, inspect the unused toilet equipment, read its instructions, find suitable storage locations, and identify the normal and emergency disposal contacts. Do not deliberately disable household plumbing or generate waste for practice. Test that the intended user can use the position and supplies safely, with normal facilities available. Hygiene with limited water Water outage When water returns, sewer service may still be damaged. Resume plumbing only once its use and disposal route are safe; arrange qualified cleanup for significant sewage contamination. Bleach does not make sewage floodwater safe to enter. Never mix cleaning chemicals. Contamination and infection risks are greater for children and immunocompromised people. If no collection is operating, contain waste securely in a protected place away from living, food and water areas while seeking a verified disposal option. Do not improvise an open discharge that endangers neighbours. Choose a stable accessible toilet position, appropriate privacy and assistance, and a safe handwashing arrangement. Plan diapers, continence care and soiled-clothing containment explicitly. Keep children and pets away from waste and contaminated areas; share cleanup responsibilities only with capable adults. no toilet sewer backup toilet no water sewage outage Water supply and wastewater service are different Set a boundary around contamination Choose a temporary toilet for the user and setting Make waste handling and handwashing one task A disposal plan is essential Restart service and review what failed Check for backup If drains or toilets back up, stop adding water and keep clear of the affected area. Do not operate electrical equipment in standing water. Keep clean supplies separate Protect drinking-water containers and food. Use a designated clean handwashing area with safe water and soap. Use a contained temporary option Use a purpose-made portable or camping toilet according to instructions, or a sturdy lidded container with appropriate leak-resistant liners as a temporary arrangement. Keep it stable and away from children. Handle waste cautiously Wear gloves when available, close liners securely and prevent leaks. Wash hands after handling and before food preparation. Keep waste away from water sources. Confirm disposal Use an established safe disposal service or locally appropriate sanitation guidance. Do not dump waste into streets, rivers, storm drains or open ground.

title: Shelter destinations: verify access before leaving
summary: Identify a destination that is actually open, reachable and suitable for your household. Ask about pets, accessibility, essential care and what to bring. A pre-storm evacuation center may have fewer supplies than a longer-term recovery shelter. Never treat an old shelter address as confirmation of current access.
text: The shelter cannot meet a care need? Arrange a suitable alternative before relying on it. Immediate danger leaves no time to pack? Take the first safe protective step; possessions come later. Does a shelter listing guarantee a space? No. Check current access and instructions with the provider, and maintain an alternate when possible. A destination record worth keeping Editorial fields: location, source of current information, check time, route, transport contact, access arrangements, pet arrangements and alternate. If you are travelling with several households, confirm that each has a transport and contact plan; do not assume the group can solve missing capacity after departure. Match your bag to the location Ask which supplies the specific site requests. Balance carryable essentials with transport limits. Keep care equipment, medicine information and contact details accessible rather than buried beneath blankets. Do not delay leaving immediate danger to complete a packing list. Check the destination again before departure when time and conditions allow. Tell your outside contact where you are going and when to expect the next check-in. Shelter services vary by location and event. The linked Florida account describes past storm arrangements; it is not a current shelter listing or a promise of beds, transport or care. If current shelter details cannot be confirmed, use other trusted current channels or a known reachable private destination where safe. Avoid travelling blindly into the hazard to investigate an old listing. Write down access, caregiver and pet needs before calling. Someone who needs specialist care may need a different arrangement from a general shelter; seek a suitable plan early. find evacuation shelter shelter packing shelter pets where to evacuate Confirm the current location Use current local emergency-management or shelter-provider information. Record the address, opening status and time you checked. Check household needs Ask about mobility access, pets, medicines and necessary equipment. Do not assume every location has the same services. Pack essentials you can carry Bring medicines, relevant medical information, hygiene items, suitable clothing, charging cables and food or bedding requested by the shelter. Keep an alternate Choose another checked destination where possible and decide how your outside contact will learn about a change.

title: Shelter-in-place
summary: Get inside if the outdoor hazard makes travel more dangerous, and choose the room for that hazard: a lowest-floor sturdy interior area for a tornado, protective interior mass for fallout, or few outside openings for an airborne chemical release. Close openings and control ventilation only as the hazard requires. Do not remain in a burning, flooding or collapsing building, and do not wait for a message when immediate danger is visible.
text: Is the basement always the best room? No. Tornado and fallout guidance often favor low or central protective areas, while CDC chemical-release guidance uses different room criteria. Identify the hazard and follow its specific instructions. Does silence mean the hazard is over? No. Loss of messages, reduced noise or absence of an odor does not establish an all-clear. Keep using an appropriate information channel and reassess actual inside conditions. The phrase does not identify the correct room Shelter-in-place means using a protective location rather than travelling through a hazard. It does not describe one universal room or ventilation setting. Identify the actual threat, affected area, building conditions, and current instructions before applying a familiar checklist. A tornado room and a chemical-release room can require different choices. Hazard-specific shelter choices Threat Main protective idea Important boundary Tornado Use a basement, safe room, or sturdy interior area away from windows Do not substitute a mobile home, tent, or large open room for appropriate shelter. Outdoor chemical release Follow the chemical instruction for a room that limits outside air CDC’s general chemical guidance favors the highest practical room; do not reuse tornado placement automatically. Radioactive fallout Put building material between people and outside fallout Use the separate nuclear/fallout guide for timing and contamination instructions. Ordinary utility interruption Maintain essential care and safe household conditions Staying home is not viable indefinitely when essential needs fail. Fire or failing building Escape the immediate building hazard A general shelter message is not permission to remain in immediate danger. This comparison is an orientation tool, not a site assessment. Read the relevant hazard guide and any applicable current instruction. Do not confidently infer which room is suitable from a floor number alone. Choose and prepare locations before the event Identify suitable spaces for the hazards that actually affect your area. Record how to reach each, how everyone can move there, which supplies are accessible, and what building systems may matter. Someone unable to use stairs may need an advance alternative rather than a last-minute promise that a high or low floor can be reached. A household shelter decision Threat Identify the hazard and the specific shelter instruction. Building Check whether the building is suitable and free from immediate internal danger. People Choose the reachable protective space and maintain essential care there. Review Follow updates and act if the shelter itself becomes unsafe. Editorial planning aid. Actual hazards, access needs and current instructions control the decision. Do a safe walk to each location and check the actual doors, furniture, and walking space. Keep the path usable without relying on powered lighting. Store a light and relevant information where they can be reached. Avoid turning the room into storage so dense that people, pets, and care equipment cannot fit. Tornado Nuclear detonation and fallout For a chemical instruction, control outside air as directed CDC’s general chemical-emergency guidance calls for getting indoors, closing windows and doors, turning off fans, air conditioning and the furnace, and moving to the chosen room. It describes temporarily sealing openings with appropriate supplies. Follow the actual incident instruction and equipment limits; this is not a general ventilation rule for every emergency. Prepare supplies and identify controls in advance if this hazard is relevant. Mark which controls belong to your dwelling and which are shared building systems. Ask management about shared ventilation before a crisis; do not dismantle unfamiliar equipment, block safety systems, or assume a room is airtight because its door closes. Never add combustion to a sealed shelter Do not use a generator, grill, outdoor stove, or improvised fuel-burning heater in the room. Sealing does not protect people from a hazard created inside the shelter. Keep an immediate escape option and seek urgent help for symptoms or another internal danger. Plastic and tape provide a temporary protective measure when the specific instruction calls for it; they are not proof of indefinite safe air or guaranteed protection. Keep following updates, and use the incident’s directions for ending the shelter period. Do not invent a universal number of hours for a sealed room. Bring essentials without delaying protection Move people and necessary assistance first. Collect medicines, essential equipment, phone power, a radio or other accessible alert source, safe water, and pet necessities only when doing so does not delay the protective action. Avoid repeatedly leaving the shelter to collect conveniences. Count everyone at entry and keep a named adult responsible for each dependent person. Choose a light that people can use safely and keep walking routes clear. Keep a concise contact message ready: location, people present, immediate needs, and next planned check-in. Place food and drinking water apart from waste and personal-care activity. Respect medicine and device instructions; ordinary supplies in the room do not replace an individual care backup. A shelter plan should include how a person receives instructions if they cannot hear an alarm, read a phone screen, or understand the language used. Arrange accessible communication rather than assuming another resident will translate or assist. A familiar comfort item may help a child if it is already available, but retrieving it must not delay sheltering. Monitor both the outside threat and the inside conditions Write down the latest instruction, its source, time, and affected area. Keep a reliable information channel available while conserving unnecessary device use. A social-media message from another neighborhood may not apply to the building or hazard you are facing. Updates can change the safer action. Conditions to reassess Change Decision to make Fire, gas, flooding, structural damage, or CO alarm inside Leave the immediate danger using appropriate escape guidance; seek help from a safe place. Essential care cannot continue Use the urgent-care or individual backup plan and communicate the need when possible. Instruction changes to evacuation Use the hazard-specific departure directions and current route information. Communication fails Use the prepared alternative; keep applying known protective steps while assessing actual conditions. No clear all-clear Do not treat silence or reduced smell as proof the hazard has ended. Avoid two extremes: staying regardless of an unsafe building, and going outside simply because waiting is uncomfortable. The decision needs the actual hazard and the household’s condition. If guidance is unavailable, retain the best known protective arrangement while watching for immediate internal danger. Ending the shelter period and improving the plan Use the applicable all-clear and recovery instructions. For a chemical incident, follow directions about leaving, ventilation, and possible exposure rather than removing seals and opening every window on a guess. Tornado recovery and fallout recovery have different hazards. A quieter street is not a universal clearance signal. Account for the household and check urgent care needs. Confirm which instruction applies to leaving the room or building. Avoid damaged utility areas, debris, or other remaining hazards. Replenish the supplies used and restore the room without obstructing exits. Record one access problem, one information problem, and any equipment misunderstanding. Update the hazard-specific room plan and explain the changes to everyone who uses it. A tabletop practice can ask which room the household would use for two different hazards and why. Keep the exercise low risk: do not deliberately seal occupied rooms, disable essential care systems, or create a ventilation problem. Finding an incorrect assumption before an emergency is the useful outcome. Plan safe rooms for the hazards in your area and keep an alert source that works during outages. Do not apply chemical room-sealing instructions to every hazard or remain in a burning building. Choose the room for the hazard, not the phrase: lowest sturdy interior area for tornadoes, protective interior mass for fallout, and a room with few outside openings for an airborne chemical threat. Leave a shelter that is burning, flooding or collapsing rather than following a generic stay-inside rule. Plan a reachable shelter space for each relevant hazard. Assign help for children, pets and anyone with mobility or communication needs; count people at entry. Keep prescribed care and an accessible alert method available. Do not assume the same room or ventilation rule is suitable for every threat. Shelter The phrase does not identify the correct room Choose and prepare locations before the event For a chemical instruction, control outside air as directed Bring essentials without delaying protection Monitor both the outside threat and the inside conditions Ending the shelter period and improving the plan Identify the hazard Read the actual shelter instruction and affected area. Choose the correct room Use an interior low room for tornadoes, a basement or central area for fallout, and the room specified for a chemical event. Bring immediate essentials Take people, pets, medicines, phone power and a radio without delaying shelter. Stay informed Remain until officials advise otherwise, unless fire or another immediate danger makes the building unsafe.

title: Small-team preparedness: roles, buddies and check-ins
summary: A small civilian team needs clear responsibilities, buddy checks, a shared destination and an agreed response to separation. Keep coordination simple enough to use when people are tired or communications fail.
text: Is buying equipment enough? No. Check that it fits the intended task, can be used by the people who need it, and has a maintenance plan. Practice in safe conditions before relying on it. A short situation update Use a repeatable message: where we are, who is present, what has changed, what we need, and the next safe action. Repeat back important details. Give one person responsibility for updating an outside contact so several conflicting messages do not create confusion. Group movement for ordinary emergencies Move at a pace the least able person can sustain and keep people together through route changes. Do not send an unwell person back alone or split the group casually. Emergency coordination is not patrol training: avoiding hazards, maintaining accountability and reaching a safe destination are the aims. Run a 15-minute departure drill. Test a missing radio, a changed driver and a dependent who needs extra time; then revise roles. This guide covers civilian coordination, not combat tactics, armed patrols, ambushes or evasion. Use the written meeting and timing plan. If radios or phones fail, keep the group together and use known safe destinations. A missing person calls for the agreed response and safe reporting, not uncontrolled searching into danger. Assign help based on actual ability, consent and care needs. Include people who cannot carry supplies or hear radio messages. Children should not carry critical responsibilities they cannot manage. Group coordination small team tactics buddy system team preparedness Name roles and backups Assign coordination, dependent care, transport, supplies and contact updates. Give every critical role a backup rather than relying on one person. Use buddy accountability Agree who checks each person is present and able to continue. Check at departures, junctions and destinations; do not silently assume someone is following. Share the same plan Write meeting points, destination, timing and communications options. Confirm everyone can explain the plan in their own words. Set stop and change rules Pause when someone is missing, injured, exhausted or unable to continue. Use safe regroup points and change the plan openly.

title: Storm surge
summary: If a storm-surge evacuation order covers you, leave for a safe location outside the surge zone before roads close. Wind strength alone does not describe surge danger. Never walk or drive through coastal floodwater.
text: What matters before collecting supplies? If a storm-surge evacuation order covers you, leave for a safe location outside the surge zone before roads close. Wind strength alone does not describe surge danger. Never walk or drive through coastal floodwater. Collect items only if doing so does not delay this action. What should another household member do? Use a second person to handle communication or dependents while the first carries out the immediate action. For storm surge, keep the specific hazard in view: Storm surge may arrive before the worst wind. Do not wait for visible water. What should be written down? Record when the situation changed, what action was taken and what remains uncertain. For this situation, start with: If trapped. Contact emergency services with your location and move to a safer higher level without entering a closed attic. Keep personal notes private; they are not submitted to Osprey Zero.  Return only after reentry is allowed; damaged bridges, debris and polluted water can remain. Storm surge may arrive before the worst wind. Do not wait for visible water. If you live in a surge zone, arrange an inland destination before the storm. Do not wait for public transport that has not been confirmed. Once roads are flooded, do not force a crossing; use the safest elevated location and signal if trapped. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: check the surge zone. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Storm surge may arrive before the worst wind. Do not wait for visible water. Tropical weather Check the surge zone Use your local emergency management evacuation map and official order. Leave early Choose an inland destination outside the evacuation area and use designated routes. Avoid shoreline viewing Stay away from beaches, seawalls and flooded coastal roads. If trapped Contact emergency services with your location and move to a safer higher level without entering a closed attic.

title: Suspected opioid overdose
summary: Unresponsiveness with slow, abnormal or absent breathing may be an opioid overdose. Call the local emergency number, give naloxone according to the product instructions if available, and begin CPR with breaths if not breathing normally. Do not delay CPR or an AED for naloxone.
text: They begin breathing normally Continue monitoring, use a recovery position when appropriate and be prepared to restart CPR if normal breathing stops. No naloxone available Continue resuscitation and seek urgent care. Do not delay CPR while searching distant locations for medicine. Does naloxone replace CPR? No. CPR and AED use remain essential when the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.  Medical evaluation is still needed after naloxone. Note dose times and changes in breathing and give this information during handover. Do not let the person “sleep it off,” put them in a cold shower or give food or drink. Naloxone is not a substitute for breathing support or urgent care. Give available naloxone and resuscitation promptly while a helper seeks care. Keep monitoring after improvement: opioids can outlast naloxone and breathing can worsen again. Stay until a capable person takes over or the scene becomes unsafe. Keep naloxone accessible wherever overdose risk exists and learn how the supplied product works. Share emergency roles without stigma; the immediate objective is breathing and medical care. Keep children and bystanders away from needles and unverified substances.  Check scene and breathing Avoid needles, powders and traffic hazards. Check responsiveness and normal breathing quickly; gasping or gurgling is not reassuring. Request help and equipment Send someone to call and bring naloxone and an AED when available. Share the exact location and breathing status. Support breathing and circulation If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR with breaths if able and trained; use an AED promptly. Give compressions if breaths are not possible. Use naloxone and observe Follow the actual device instructions, including repeat dosing. Do not interrupt CPR to wait for a response. If normal breathing returns, place on their side as appropriate and keep monitoring.

title: Suspected stroke
summary: Sudden facial droop, arm weakness or speech trouble may be a stroke. Call the local emergency number immediately, note when symptoms began or the person was last well, and stay with them. Symptoms that disappear still need urgent medical evaluation.
text: If symptoms stop Keep the request for urgent evaluation active; write when symptoms resolved. Do not cancel care based on improvement alone. If communication fails Use a written location and symptom timeline for a trusted relay. Keep the patient accompanied rather than sending them alone to find a signal. Is this heat stroke? This page concerns a sudden neurological emergency. Heat illness needs immediate cooling; see Extreme heat. Search results cannot distinguish the cause of confusion.  Pass the symptom timeline to the receiving clinician. Even a brief episode or apparent recovery needs urgent assessment. Do not assume FAST rules out stroke; children and some adults have other symptoms. Do not use aspirin as stroke treatment without clinical direction. Keep attempting to reach urgent medical care while watching breathing and responsiveness. Tell a trusted person the exact location and last-known-well time. Do not make the affected person walk or drive. An inaccessible ambulance service does not make home observation a treatment. Speech difficulty can prevent a person from telling others what they need. Use short questions, allow time and avoid asking them to repeat a long history. Keep children with another adult, clear access and prepare the medication list for handover.  Recognize sudden changes Use FAST: Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to act. Sudden loss of balance, vision changes or severe headache can also matter. Record the time Write down symptom onset or the last time the person was known well. Do not delay seeking care while completing a checklist. Protect breathing Keep them comfortable. If not fully awake but breathing, place on their side when safe. Do not give food, drink or medication to someone with swallowing difficulty. Watch responsiveness If unresponsive and not breathing normally, begin CPR and use an AED. Follow dispatcher instructions when available.

title: Thunderstorm
summary: Go inside a substantial building or a fully enclosed hard-top vehicle when thunder is heard. Stay away from windows and monitor warnings for damaging wind, hail, tornadoes and flash flooding.
text: What matters before collecting supplies? Go inside a substantial building or a fully enclosed hard-top vehicle when thunder is heard. Stay away from windows and monitor warnings for damaging wind, hail, tornadoes and flash flooding. Collect items only if doing so does not delay this action. What should another household member do? Use a second person to handle communication or dependents while the first carries out the immediate action. For thunderstorm, keep the specific hazard in view: Every thunderstorm can produce lightning, even without a severe thunderstorm warning. What should be written down? Record when the situation changed, what action was taken and what remains uncertain. For this situation, start with: Wait before returning. After the last thunder, wait at least 30 minutes before resuming outdoor activity. Keep personal notes private; they are not submitted to Osprey Zero.  Check for downed lines and flooded routes before travel. Schedule outdoor work around forecasts. Every thunderstorm can produce lightning, even without a severe thunderstorm warning. Use a substantial building or enclosed hard-top vehicle even when warnings cannot be checked. Avoid plumbing and wired electrical equipment during lightning. Watch for rising water and damaging wind without going outside to observe the storm. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: get indoors. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Every thunderstorm can produce lightning, even without a severe thunderstorm warning. Severe storms Get indoors Open shelters, tents and trees do not protect from lightning. Avoid conductive paths Inside, avoid plumbing and plugged-in equipment during lightning. Read new warnings Move to an interior room for severe wind or hail; use a tornado shelter if a tornado warning is issued. Wait before returning After the last thunder, wait at least 30 minutes before resuming outdoor activity.

title: Tornado
summary: If a tornado warning covers your location, shelter now in a basement or small interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. Stay away from windows and cover your head and neck. A mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter.
text: What if there is no basement? Identify an interior room on the lowest usable floor of a substantial building, away from windows. Plan the shortest route there before a warning. Protect the head and neck with available protection; equipment retrieval must not delay shelter. What if I am in a mobile home? A mobile home is not a tornado shelter even when tied down. Arrange a nearby substantial shelter before storms arrive and move while there is safe time. Do not wait for visible damage to decide that a different location is needed.  Afterward, avoid damaged buildings, broken glass and downed lines. Check for injuries and use text to let your contact know you are safe. Do not wait to see a funnel. Darkness and rain can hide tornadoes. A watch calls for readiness; a warning calls for action. Go to your identified shelter without waiting for confirmation when a warning or nearby clear danger is present. Keep shoes, a light and head protection close. If in a mobile home, use a nearby sturdy shelter before conditions worsen; never attempt to outrun a tornado in traffic. Choose a shelter that can actually fit and be reached by everyone. Keep shoes, a light and necessary mobility aids nearby; supervise children and secure pets without blocking the route. Rehearse how a person who cannot hear warnings will be notified. Severe storms Go to the shelter Move immediately; put shoes on if within reach and take your phone without delaying. Use a designated storm shelter when accessible. Protect your head Crouch low and cover your head and neck with your arms. Use a sturdy table or available cushioning for additional protection. If outside or in a vehicle Get to a nearby sturdy building if safely possible. Do not shelter under an overpass. Vehicles and mobile homes offer little protection. Keep listening Use local warning messages or weather radio; remain sheltered until the threat has passed and official updates permit leaving.

title: Trailer, RV and mobile-home preparedness
summary: Plan early access to a sturdy shelter and a safe destination. A trailer, RV or mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter; supplies and tie-downs do not change that limitation.

Follow equipment-specific guidance for filters, dispensers, and any affected private-well system. Keep restricted-use water clearly separated until it is no longer needed or has been disposed of appropriately. Replenish the stored drinking-water reserve and record what the household actually used. If water remains unusual or the situation is unclear, use the suitable alternative and seek further guidance through a safe, reachable channel. Record which supplies, labels, carrying arrangements, or contacts would make the next outage easier. Build an emergency water supply and know how your household will handle sanitation. Do not use heating-system or radiator water for drinking. Inventory clean containers and safe water, then prioritise drinking, food, medicines and hand hygiene. Do not use nonpotable water in food or formula. Plan toilet and waste arrangements separately and keep them away from food and water storage. Give one person responsibility for clean drinking-water containers and another for dirty water or sanitation. Keep containers manageable for the person who must lift them; avoid unmarked bottles accessible to young children. Water Identify the problem before using another source Keep drinking-quality water for the right tasks Calculate what you have and when you need more Handle a boil-water notice correctly Manage hygiene and toilet needs separately Resupply without turning the trip into another problem When service returns: wait for clearance and follow the reset Find the notice Check the affected address, restoration estimate and any advisory. Prioritize safe water Reserve approved water for drinking, medications, formula, food and pets. Plan hygiene Use local health instructions for sanitation and safe handwashing without running water. Wait for clearance Follow flushing and treatment instructions once the utility restores service.

title: Water purification
summary: Use safe bottled water when available. For microbial risk, bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet, and cool before use. Water contaminated with fuel, chemicals or radioactive material cannot be made safe by boiling or ordinary disinfection.
text: Does clear water mean safe water? No. Clarity does not show whether germs, fuel, pesticides or other chemicals are present. Select the safest source available and identify suspected contamination before choosing treatment. Boiling or ordinary filtration does not resolve every chemical hazard. What if the label differs from an online recipe? Follow the exact treatment product instructions for the water condition, volume and contact time. Do not mix products or estimate a stronger dose. A device’s microbial claims and maintenance requirements must match the actual task.  Store treated water in clean covered containers and prevent recontamination. Clear water can still contain germs. Ordinary filters may not remove viruses or chemicals. Choose the least contaminated available source and establish whether the problem is microbial or chemical. If the source may contain fuel, industrial chemicals or radioactive material, find another source; a camping filter or boiling is not a universal solution. Keep untreated and treated water in different labeled containers. Use clean utensils and teach each person how safe water is dispensed. Plan extra care for infant feeding and people with weakened immunity; a field filter is not automatically suitable for every medical use. Water Check the source Avoid floodwater or sources suspected of toxic contamination; find an approved alternative. Clarify cloudy water Let sediment settle or strain through a clean cloth before treatment; this alone does not disinfect it. Boil for germs Use the appropriate time and cool safely in a clean container. If boiling is unavailable Use a treatment product as labeled and official guidance for your water source; filters have different capabilities.

title: When authorities are unsafe to approach
summary: If contacting an official could expose you or your family to harm, prioritise immediate physical safety and use trusted private contacts or independently verified humanitarian and local legal support when safe. Do not publish sensitive locations or confront armed personnel. Keep essential documents and a realistic shelter or relocation plan.
text: If contacting an official could expose you or your family to harm, prioritise immediate physical safety and use trusted private contacts or independently verified humanitarian and local legal support when safe. title: Wildfire
summary: Check evacuation notices for your address. Leave promptly when ordered, using the current official route; do not delay for possessions. If a fire threatens your escape or you are trapped, call emergency services with your precise location.
text: When should a household with access needs leave? Arrange transport, medicine, pets and equipment before routes become crowded or smoky. Leaving early can reduce the difficulty of moving a person who needs extra time; verify the route and destination rather than relying on a single notification. Can a respirator make a road safe? No. A particle respirator does not protect against heat, every gas or a blocked road. Smoke protection is one part of the decision; active fire, access and changing wind can make travel unsafe regardless of a mask.  Return only when reentry is allowed. Check for damaged utilities, hot debris and continuing smoke. A smoke-control room cannot protect you from a fire approaching the building. Leave before the only usable route is threatened. If no official update is reachable, act on visible nearby fire, rapidly worsening conditions and verified local information rather than waiting for an order. Do not drive into smoke with unknown visibility or through flames. Assign one person to dependents and pets and another to transport and contacts. Keep essential medicine, access aids and car keys together. Agree on a reunion place that is outside the threatened area, with a second option if access changes. Fire & air Confirm your zone Use fire agency and emergency management alerts rather than old perimeter maps. Gather people and pets Take essential medicines, identification, keys and phone power without delaying departure. Use official routes Smoke and closures can change quickly; do not drive into heavy smoke or flames. Report your destination Tell an out-of-area contact where you are going and follow shelter instructions.

title: Wildfire smoke
summary: For smoke without an immediate fire threat, stay indoors with windows and doors closed, use filtered recirculated air or a portable air cleaner, and check local air-quality updates. If ordered to evacuate, leave promptly. Severe breathing difficulty requires emergency medical help.
text: Separate an approaching fire from a smoke exposure problem.  What if closing windows makes the home too hot? Smoke reduction must be balanced with safe temperature. Check a cooler location with cleaner air and the ability to meet medical or access needs. Do not keep a vulnerable person in dangerous heat simply to preserve a closed room. Can any mask filter smoke? Loose face coverings do not provide the same particle protection as a well-fitting approved respirator. Particle respirators do not remove gases and may not fit children or everyone who needs one. Reduce exposure and seek medical guidance for breathing problems.  Keep checking changing wind, fire perimeter, and air-quality conditions. People with heart or lung disease, children, older adults, and pregnant people may need added precautions or clinical advice. If fire threatens the building or officials order departure, indoor smoke control is no substitute for evacuation. If breathing becomes difficult or symptoms are severe, seek urgent medical help. Create one cleaner-air room using safe filtration if available, reduce indoor smoke sources and avoid strenuous activity. Do not overheat a sealed home; move to a safer breathable and cooler place if you cannot maintain both air quality and safe temperature. Check people with lung or heart disease, pregnancy-related needs and infants more often. Plan low-exposure activities and keep prescribed medicines accessible. A designated cleaner room must still be comfortable, reachable and usable for the people inside. Fire & air Know which problem you face Check official fire, evacuation, and air-quality notices for your address. An evacuation order changes the decision immediately. If leaving, leave early Take people, pets, medication, keys, and essentials; tell a contact where you are going. Use the evacuation guide and current route instructions. If sheltering from smoke Close windows and doors. Set HVAC to recirculate where possible, use a portable air cleaner or a cleaner indoor room, and avoid adding indoor smoke from candles, frying, or smoking. Limit outside exposure If you must go outside in smoke, a well-fitting N95 or P100 respirator can reduce particle exposure; ordinary cloth masks do not provide the same protection.

title: Winter storm
summary: Stay indoors and postpone travel during dangerous snow, ice or blowing snow. Keep heat safe, use battery lighting and watch for power loss. If stranded in a vehicle, stay with it unless a safer shelter is clearly accessible.

Do not walk away from a stranded vehicle in poor visibility unless you know a safe nearby destination. Keep dry layers, safe food, water and battery light together. If stranded in a vehicle, keep the exhaust clear before running the engine and conserve fuel; do not sleep with the engine running. Remain with the vehicle when walking would expose you to poor visibility or severe cold. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
